Cleanup uses cancellation-independent contexts, preserves recreated entries and child indexes, and uses compare-and-delete checks to avoid deleting concurrent updates. ### Changes **Redis directory cleanup** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Orphaned index repair**
`weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go`, `weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store_test.go`|Directory listing removes missing-entry index members. Repair skips super-large directories and restores members when entries or child indexes still exist. Tests cover recreated entries, child directories, and super-large directories.| |**Race-safe expiration cleanup**
`weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go`, `weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store_test.go`|Logical expiration uses a shared predicate. Expired entries are re-read and compare-and-deleted only when their bytes remain unchanged. Tests cover logical expiration, recreated values, and compare-and-delete results. Test cleanup now reports Redis close and deletion errors.| **Estimated code review effort:** 4 (Complex) | ~45 minutes **Mergeability Score:** _🔵 Low_ · up to `a2d72` The change protects recreated values during logical-expiry cleanup, but a narrow race with physical Redis expiry can still leave a stale directory-index member until a later listing repairs it. # Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

Greptile Summary

 The PR makes logical-expiry cleanup conditional on the value bytes that were rechecked, preventing cleanup from deleting a concurrent recreation. - Extracts the logical-expiry predicate for consistent initial and repeated checks. - Adds a single-key compare-and-delete script compatible with Redis Cluster. - Routes post-delete index cleanup through the existing orphan-repair helper. - Adds coverage for logical expiration, recreated values, key prefixes, and compare-and-delete outcomes.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 The PR appears safe to merge. No blocking failure remains.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go | Adds a rechecked, byte-conditional logical-expiry deletion path and race-aware directory-index cleanup without leaving an eligible unresolved defect. | | weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store_test.go | Adds Redis-backed tests for logical expiration, recreation preservation, key-prefix handling, and all compare-and-delete script results. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant L as Directory listing participant V as Redis value key participant S as Compare-delete script participant I as Directory index L->>V: Re-read entry bytes V-->>L: Current bytes L->>L: Decode and recheck logical expiry L->>S: Delete only if bytes still match S->>V: Atomic GET and conditional DEL alt Value changed by recreation S-->>L: 0 (preserve value and index) else Value deleted or unchanged S-->>L: -1 or 1 L->>I: Remove orphaned member and repair races end ```
